info.title: Apex Trading
info.description:
## Responsible Use

Integrators, please take the time to efficiently design your API queries. This is considerate of our server load, and also will reduce the API fees your company or the companies you are working with may be charged. Call our API as much as appropriate, but be considerate.

Some API endpoints require an `updated_at_from` field to be set in the query. The first time you call the endpoint you should call it from the date the company first joined, but subsequent calls should be restricted to only search for records updated since the last call.

**Example Daily Inventory Sync** — getting data that changed in the last 24 hours:

| Day | Products Request | Batches Request |
|-----|-----------------|-----------------|
| Day 1 (2025-04-21) | `/products?updated_at_from=2025-04-20T22:00:00Z` | `/batches?updated_at_from=2025-04-20T22:00:00Z` |
| Day 2 (2025-04-22) | `/products?updated_at_from=2025-04-21T22:00:00Z` | `/batches?updated_at_from=2025-04-21T22:00:00Z` |
| Day 3 (2025-04-23) | `/products?updated_at_from=2025-04-22T22:00:00Z` | `/batches?updated_at_from=2025-04-22T22:00:00Z` |

---

## Rate Limiting

All API requests are subject to rate limiting to ensure fair usage and service stability.

**15 requests per second** per API token.

Every response includes headers indicating your current rate limit status:

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 15
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 10
```

When you exceed the rate limit, you will receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1699564823
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0

{ "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Maximum 15 requests per second allowed." }
```

**Best Practices:**
- **Implement exponential backoff** — when you receive a 429, wait before retrying.
- **Respect Retry-After** — wait the specified number of seconds before your next request.
- **Spread requests** — avoid synchronized operations (e.g., all cron jobs at :00). Choose random times for your syncs to minimize the thundering herd problem.
- **Cache responses** — reduce unnecessary API calls by caching data locally.

---

## API Completeness

The API provides a subset of the features in the application. We add to it by request.

---

## API Credits

Every API call is billed as follows:

- **1 credit** per request.
- Plus credits per item in the response:
  - **1 credit per item** on most endpoints.
  - **3 credits per item** on data-heavy endpoints (listed below).
- Plus **1 credit per nested item** when you opt into related data via certain `with_*` flags.

### Examples

| Request | What you receive | Math | Credits |
|---------|------------------|------|---------|
| `GET /cannabinoids` | 20 cannabinoids | 1 + 20 × 1 | **21** |
| `GET /products` | 5 products | 1 + (5 × 3) | **16** |
| `GET /products?with_batches=true` | 5 products with 10 batches | 1 + (5 × 3) + (10 × 1) | **26** |
| `GET /buyers` | 200 buyers | 1 + (200 × 3) | **601** |
| `GET /buyers?with_contacts=true` | 200 buyers with 800 contacts | 1 + (200 × 3) + (800 × 1) | **1,401** |
| `GET /shipping-orders/{id}` | 1 order | 1 + (1 × 3) | **4** |

### Data-Heavy Endpoints (3 credits per item)

`/available-inventory` · `/buyer/{id}` · `/buyers` · `/product/{id}` · `/products` · `/receiving-orders` · `/shipping-order/{id}` · `/shipping-orders` · `/transporter-order/{id}` · `/transporter-orders`

Every other endpoint bills at the default rate of 1 credit per item returned.

### Chargeable `with_*` Flags (1 credit per nested item)

When set to `true`, each of these flags charges 1 credit per item in the loaded collection.

- **Batches:** `with_cannabinoids`, `with_terpenes`, `with_history`
- **Buyer Groups:** `with_buyers`
- **Buyer Leads:** `with_notes`
- **Buyers:** `with_contacts`, `with_contact_logs`, `with_notes`, `with_sales_reps`, `with_tags`
- **Deal Flows:** `with_documents`, `with_order_statuses`
- **Product Categories:** `with_types`
- **Products:** `with_batches`, `with_metrc`, `with_history`
- **Receiving Orders:** `with_items`, `with_payments`, `with_history`
- **Shipping Orders:** `with_items`, `with_payments`, `with_history`
- **Transporter Orders:** `with_items`, `with_payments`

> ⚠️ **Heads up.** `with_contact_logs` (on `/buyers`) and `with_history` (on `/products`, `/batches`, `/shipping-orders`, `/receiving-orders`) commonly return thousands of nested rows per parent. Pulling them in bulk is the fastest way to run up credits — leave them off unless you specifically need that data, or fetch them per-record via the singular detail endpoint when you do.

### Free `with_*` Flags (included in base price)

These pull single-row dimensional data and don't add to your bill:

`with_state`, `with_country`, `with_brand`, `with_category`, `with_product_type`, `with_operation`, `with_stage`, `with_term`, `with_pricing_tier`, `with_buyer_company`, `with_deal_flow`.

### Monthly Cost Example: External Sync Integrator

Estimated monthly credits for an integrator polling every 30 minutes to keep an external data source in sync. Assumes **products fetched 3×**, **batches 30×**, and **orders 3×** per month per record (each row is touched that many times during the month as updates flow through), with `with_items=true` on orders.

| Your size | Base requests | Products | Batches | Orders + Items | Total / month |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ~25 orders/month | 4,320 | 81 | 4,320 | 1,350 | **10,071** |
| ~100 orders/month | 4,320 | 315 | 17,310 | 5,400 | **27,345** |
| ~300 orders/month | 4,320 | 945 | 51,900 | 16,200 | **73,365** |
| ~700 orders/month | 4,320 | 2,214 | 121,080 | 37,800 | **165,414** |

Applied to a **100,000 credit/month** allowance (your plan's allowance may be higher or lower) at **$0.0002/credit** overage:

| Your size | Total credits | Over allowance | Cost on your plan |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ~25 orders/month | 10,071 | 0 | **$0.00/month** |
| ~100 orders/month | 27,345 | 0 | **$0.00/month** |
| ~300 orders/month | 73,365 | 0 | **$0.00/month** |
| ~700 orders/month | 165,414 | 65,414 | **$13.08/month** |

### For Contrast: Bad Integrator

Same customer sizes and polling schedule, but the integrator **does not use `updated_at_from`** (every poll returns the entire dataset, not just changes) and pulls **`with_history=true`** on each order's detail. This is what your bill looks like when an integration isn't built to the recommended practices:

| Your size | Total credits / month | Cost on your plan |
|---|---:|---:|
| ~25 orders/month | 899,564 | **$159.91/month** |
| ~100 orders/month | 3,582,416 | **$696.48/month** |
| ~300 orders/month | 10,737,168 | **$2,127.43/month** |
| ~700 orders/month | 25,050,993 | **$4,990.20/month** |

The single biggest contributor is the missing `updated_at_from` — every poll re-fetches all data instead of just what changed. The fix is one query parameter.

### Monthly Allowance and Spending Cap

Your account includes a monthly free credit allowance. Usage beyond the allowance is billed at your plan's per-credit overage rate. See your usage and billing history from the API management page.

A **spending cap** controls the maximum monthly overage spend. If your spending cap is $0, requests that would exceed your free allowance are rejected with a `429` response. Set a spending cap from your account settings to allow overage usage.

### Keeping Your Bill Low

- Always use the `updated_at_from` parameter on list endpoints. Otherwise you re-fetch the full dataset on every call and pay for it.
- Don't poll faster than your business actually changes. Most inventory and CRM data doesn't need sub-minute refresh.
- Use chargeable `with_*` flags to fetch everything you need in one call — it's cheaper than making N follow-up requests per record.
- Set a spending cap in your account settings to bound your maximum exposure.
- Set a credit cap per API token to bound exposure per integration.

---

## Authentication

The API will only establish communication over HTTPS and requires a valid token using **Bearer authentication**.

All API requests must include:
- **Authorization** header: `Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE`
- **Accept** header: `application/json`

All API endpoints use JSON format for sending and receiving data. All POST and PUT requests are expected to contain JSON.

If you receive HTML back in your response, this likely means you are not including the correct headers in your request.

---

## Pagination

The API uses pagination to return records. The default is **15 records per page**.

Override with the `per_page` query parameter. The maximum allowed is **500 records** for most resources. Some resources may have a smaller maximum.

Each paginated response includes `links` and `meta` objects:

```json
{
    "links": {
        "first": "https://example.com/api/v1/buyers?page=1",
        "last": "https://example.com/api/v1/buyers?page=6",
        "prev": null,
        "next": "https://example.com/api/v1/buyers?page=2"
    },
    "meta": {
        "current_page": 1,
        "from": 1,
        "last_page": 6,
        "path": "https://example.com/api/v1/buyers",
        "per_page": 15,
        "to": 15,
        "total": 85
    }
}
```

---

## Server Responses

| Code | Status | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| 200 | OK | The request has succeeded. |
| 201 | Created | The request has succeeded and a new record has been created. |
| 401 | Unauthorized | `{ "message": "Unauthenticated." }` |
| 403 | Forbidden | `{ "message": "This action is unauthorized." }` |
| 404 | Not Found | `{ "message": "Resource Not Found" }` |
| 409 | Conflict | `{ "message": "Conflict with requested update" }` |
| 422 | Unprocessable Entity | `{ "message": "The given data was invalid." }` |
| 500 | Internal Server Error | `{ "message": "Server Error" }` |

For all create and update actions the response will include the updated resource. For delete actions, a response status of 200 confirms successful deletion. The message may provide additional details on why an action is denied.

---

## Permissions

The API is gated by the resources each token is granted access to. The `/welcome` endpoint will display a list of the token permissions. We suggest that you provide the minimum necessary permissions for each API token.

---

## Post / Patch Requests

**In Post Requests:**
- **required** — you must supply this field.
- **optional** — you do not need to supply this field; it will be NULL or false if omitted.

**In Patch Requests (Sparse Updates):**

If you do not include a field in your request it will not be touched, leaving it as it was. If you do include a field but it is not set, it will be set to NULL in the database.

- **optional, not nullable** — you don't need to send it, but if you do it must have a value.
- **optional, nullable** — you don't need to send it. If you send an empty value the field will be set to NULL.

---

## Data Type Conventions

### Company ID

The root resource for accounts is called a **company**. The token will resolve to this company, and many models have a `company_id` column. Some models may have multiple — for example, orders have `buyer_company_id` and `seller_company_id`, and buyers have `buyer_company_id` (the buyer account, optionally null) and `owning_company_id` (the seller).

Some models may be optionally scoped to a `company_id`. For example, Environmental Issues has a `company_id` column. All companies have access to records where `company_id` is null, plus any records matching their own company ID. This allows us to provide defaults for everyone and specific options for individual companies.

### Array Format Requests

Many endpoints allow you to filter by an array. The query parameter will look like `ids[]` or `operation_ids[]`, which allows you to chain multiple values: `ids[]=1&ids[]=2`.

### Currency

All currency data returned is rounded to the hundredth decimal (1.00) with no symbol. When sending currency values, do not include the currency symbol or commas. You can send with or without the decimal point (100 or 100.00).

### Times and Dates

All date and date/time fields submitted to the server are expected to be in **ISO 8601** format. Likewise, all dates returned by the server will be in ISO 8601 format. The only supported date format is `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Most dates returned by the application will be in **UTC** time. Exceptions will be noted per endpoint.

| Example | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `2021-04-20` | April 20th, 2021 |
| `2021-04-20T22:04:50Z` | April 20th, 2021 10:04:50 PM UTC (Z identifier) |
| `2021-04-20T22:04:50+00:00` | Same as above using numerical offset |
| `2021-11-02T16:30:40.345+00:00` | November 2nd, 2021 4:30:40.345 PM UTC with milliseconds |
| `2021-01-12T22:20:30.456-06:00` | January 12th, 2021 10:20:30.456 PM MDT with milliseconds |

---

## Support

- **API questions:** api@apextrading.com
- **All other issues:** support@apextrading.com

get.description:
**Required ability:** `view:available-inventory`

Returns your company's own available inventory — this endpoint does not provide access to
other companies' inventory. Products are filtered to only those that are listed to buyers,
not archived, and have eligible batches with inventory.

**Filtering:**
- `product_category_id` / `product_category_ids`: filter by one or multiple product categories
- `brand_id` / `brand_ids`: filter by one or multiple brands
- `brand_name`: partial match on brand name
- `product_name`: partial match on product name
- `cultivar_name`: partial match on cultivar name
- `operation_ids`: filter to products with batches in specific seller operations
- `industry`: filter by `Med` or `Rec`
- `price_min` / `price_max`: filter by listing price range (in cents)
- `in_stock_only`: exclude pre-order items
- `pre_order_only`: only pre-order items
- `featured_only`: only featured products
- `potency_unit` + `potency_min` + `potency_max`: filter by cannabinoid potency range. `potency_unit` is `%` or `Mg`

**Sorting:**
- `sort_by`: one of `name`, `listing_price`, `category`, `brand`
- `sort_direction`: `asc` or `desc`

**Batch details:**
- `include_batches`: when `true`, each product includes its individual batches with per-batch pricing variants. Useful for batch-level ordering. When `false` (default), only product-level data is returned.

**Ordering rules driven by this endpoint:** each batch's `hold` and `sort_order` fields control
the sequence in which a buyer may consume inventory:
- `hold = false` (**off-deck**) — in-stock batches, sell first
- `hold = true` (**on-deck**) — reserved batches, may only be sold once all off-deck inventory
  for the same product has been claimed (depleted in the DB or fully claimed in the cart)

Within each pool, batches must be consumed in ascending `sort_order`. The cart endpoints
enforce this at convert time — see **Add Items to Cart** for the full rules.

**Buyer context:**
- `buyer_id`: when provided, pricing reflects the buyer's pricing tier. If the buyer has no tier, the company's marketplace tier is used. Also enforces state restrictions for cannabis.

**Pagination:**
- `per_page`: results per page (default 15, max 100). Response includes standard Laravel pagination links.

get.description:
**Required ability:** `view:batches`

Our application has a parent child relationship with inventory. There is a parent product with many child
batches. The batches are connected to the parent through a `product_id` on the batch.

A batch belongs to an operation. This is a licensed location where it is located.

A batch has a `listing_price` that applies to all batches except for batches that have a product with a
category of Pack To Order. Pack To Order batches use specific prices that correspond to weights, eg:
`pto_oneg_listing_price`, `pto_twog_listing_price`, etc.

- `listing_price_base_unit`: listing price for an individual unit of a batch sold in cases
- `minimum_sales_price`: note for sales reps on how low a batch may be sold for
- `minimum_sales_price_base_unit`: same as above, but for an individual unit of a batch sold in cases
- `disable_inventory_tracking`: set the batch to an infinite quantity
- `true_hold`: prevents a batch from being listed for sale
- `restricted`: only users with the permission to sell restricted inventory can sell this batch
- `hold`: this is an ondeck item. It is waiting for other batches to sell out before being marked for sale. It may be taken off deck automatically. You may not mark a batch as hold if no other batches are available for sale
- `pre-order`: this is an item that is not currently in inventory, but can be ordered in advance and fulfilled at a later date
- `pull_sample_from_alternative_batch_id`: rarely needed, you can take a sample from a different batch if this is set

Batches have many terpenes and cannabinoids. On the batch relation itself you will see the fields
`predominate_canabinoid_min_or_only`, `predominate_canabinoid_max`, and `predominate_canabinoid_unit`.
These relate to the predominate cannabinoid that is defined at the product level.
`predominate_canabinoid_max` can be added if there is a range, else only `predominate_canabinoid_min_or_only`
is used.

Pass the entire list of cannabinoids and terpenes on update and create. On update, any cannabinoids or
terpenes not included will be removed.

`updated_at_from` is a required filter. The first time you call this endpoint you should call it from the
date the company first joined, but subsequent calls should be restricted to only search for records updated
since the last call if possible.

post.description:
**Required ability:** `update:batches`

Available fields are gated by the product category and sometimes also by the product type. Please see the
Batch Field Rules endpoint for the field logic. This will return an allow and deny list as the specifics
for each field can be fairly complicated. If you pass in a field that is not supported, we will ignore it
and accept the other fields.

put.description:
**Required ability:** `update:batches`

`product_id` and `operation_id` are not editable. Available fields are gated by the product category and
sometimes also by the product type. Please see the Batch Field Rules endpoint for the field logic. If you
pass in a field that is not supported, we will ignore it and accept the other fields.

get.description:
**Required ability:** `view:buyers`

Contact logs do not update the `updated_at` field on the buyer. If you need to sync contact logs, query
them separately.

By default contact logs will return all contact logs that belong to your account. You may scope down to a
specific buyer by including the `buyer_id`.

`updated_at_from` is a required filter. The first time you call this endpoint you should call it from the
date the company first joined, but subsequent calls should be restricted to only search for records updated
since the last call if possible.

**Required ability:** `view:buyers`

`updated_at_from` is a required filter. The first time you call this endpoint you should call it from the
date the company first joined, but subsequent calls should be restricted to only search for records updated
since the last call if possible.

**Required ability:** `view:buyers`

Buyers are a company's CRM relation of a purchaser. The buyer may or may not have an account. If they do,
the `buyer_company_id` is set.

- `owning_company_id`: the seller's company id, the owner of the api token
- `buyer_company_id`: the buyer's company id
- `vendor_disabled`: the buyer no longer wants to work with this company
- `disabled`: the buyer has been disabled on the seller's side

A buyer has multiple child relationships: contacts, contact logs, and notes.

Updating notes and contacts will update the `updated_at` field on the buyer to allow you to easily build
a sync. Contact logs do not update the `updated_at` field on the buyer. If you need to sync contact logs,
query them separately.

A buyer also belongs to a group through a `buyer_group_id`. This allows you to group multiple different
buyers under one organization.

`updated_at_from` is a required filter. The first time you call this endpoint you should call it from the
date the company first joined, but subsequent calls should be restricted to only search for records updated
since the last call if possible.

**Required ability:** `view:products`

Container types are not available for every category of product. Please see the product field rules endpoint.

post.description:
**Required ability:** `update:products`

A `product_category_id` is required. Please see the Product Categories endpoint. Container Types are also
not shown for every product category.

put.description:
**Required ability:** `update:products`

Changing the category a container type belongs to is not permitted.

get.description:
**Required ability:** `view:dealflows`

A deal flow is a process that a company follows when handling an order. A company can have multiple
different deal flows.

A deal flow is made of many different `order_statuses` that each have a parent status. The `order_statuses`
are dynamic and can differ even within a company, however the parent status will be static across all deal
flows: Submitted, Accepted, Pending Shipment, In Transit, Delivered, Complete.

Each deal flow is required to have at least 1 `order_status` for each parent status, but can have many.

A common need is to set the status of an order, for example when it has been delivered. Since order statuses
are dynamic, we recommend taking the first `order_status_id` that exists for a given parent. E.g., to mark
an order as 'delivered', get the deal flow for the order, filter for `order_statuses` where
`parent_status.name = 'Delivered'`, sort by position and select the first.

**Required ability:** `create:marketplace-orders`

Returns purchasable inventory across all marketplace-live sellers.
Product-level prices are the sellers' listed prices; batch pricing
variants (returned when `include_batches` is `true`) are priced for your
company — your assigned pricing tier per seller where one exists, the
seller's marketplace tier otherwise. Requires marketplace API access
to be enabled for your company. This is not enabled by default. If you are interested
in this feature we require you to sign data usage agreements with us.
Please reach out to support if you are interested.

**Cross-company access:**
- `company_ids`: scope results to specific companies. When omitted, returns inventory across
  all marketplace-live seller companies on the platform. Companies that are not marketplace-eligible
  are never returned, even when explicitly requested.

**Filtering:**
- `product_category_id` / `product_category_ids`: filter by one or multiple product categories
- `brand_id` / `brand_ids`: filter by one or multiple brands
- `brand_name`: partial match on brand name
- `product_name`: partial match on product name
- `cultivar_name`: partial match on cultivar name
- `operation_ids`: filter to products with batches in specific seller operations
- `industry`: filter by `Med` or `Rec`
- `price_min` / `price_max`: filter by listing price range (in cents)
- `in_stock_only`: exclude pre-order items
- `pre_order_only`: only pre-order items
- `featured_only`: only featured products
- `potency_unit` + `potency_min` + `potency_max`: filter by cannabinoid potency range. `potency_unit` is `%` or `Mg`

**Sorting:**
- `sort_by`: one of `name`, `listing_price`, `category`, `brand`
- `sort_direction`: `asc` or `desc`

**Batch details:**
- `include_batches`: when `true`, each product includes its individual batches with per-batch
  pricing variants priced for your company. When `false` (default), only product-level data is
  returned, priced at the sellers' listed prices.

**Pagination:**
- `per_page`: results per page (default and max 100).

**Required ability:** `create:marketplace-orders`

Returns all marketplace carts belonging to the authenticated API token, one per seller.

- `per_page`: (optional) results per page, default 15, max 500

Requires marketplace API access to be enabled for your company. This is not enabled by
default — contact support to enable marketplace ordering.

**Required ability:** `create:marketplace-orders`

Returns the cart with full pricing calculations for the seller it belongs to, including
per-item pricing, subtotals, and availability status.

Requires marketplace API access to be enabled for your company. This is not enabled by
default — contact support to enable marketplace ordering.

delete.description:
**Required ability:** `create:marketplace-orders`

Permanently deletes the cart and all its items. This action cannot be undone.

Requires marketplace API access to be enabled for your company. This is not enabled by
default — contact support to enable marketplace ordering.

post.description:
**Required ability:** `create:marketplace-orders`

Adds one or more batches to your marketplace carts. Items are grouped by seller — if no
cart exists yet for a batch's seller, one is created automatically. Each API token has at
most one cart per seller.

Use the **Browse Marketplace** endpoint with `include_batches=true` to find batch
ids and their available `order_unit_measurement_id` pricing variants before adding items.

- `buyer_operation_id`: (optional) the operation these items are ordered for. Defaults to
  your company's first active operation. Must belong to your company.
- `items`: array of items to add
- `items.*.batch_id`: the batch to add
- `items.*.quantity`: amount to add. If the same (batch, sample, unit) combo already exists
  in the cart for that seller, the quantity is added to the existing item.
- `items.*.sample`: when `true`, the item is marked as a sample.
- `items.*.order_unit_measurement_id`: the unit of measurement for ordering (e.g. Case,
  Unit, Gram). Must match a valid pricing variant for the batch. Available variants are
  returned by the Browse Marketplace endpoint when `include_batches` is `true`.

Requires marketplace API access to be enabled for your company. This is not enabled by
default — contact support to enable marketplace ordering.

delete.description:
**Required ability:** `create:marketplace-orders`

Removes one or more items from the cart by cart item id. The entire item is removed
regardless of quantity — there is no partial quantity removal.

Cart item ids are returned on every line in the View Cart and Add Items responses
(`data.cart_items.*.id`). Use those values here.

- `items`: array of items to remove
- `items.*.id`: the cart item id to remove

Requires marketplace API access to be enabled for your company. This is not enabled by
default — contact support to enable marketplace ordering.

post.description:
**Required ability:** `create:marketplace-orders`

Converts the cart into one or more orders with the seller. Items are grouped by seller
operation — each group becomes a separate order. All orders are created atomically: if
any order fails, the entire conversion is rolled back.

**Pre-conversion validation:**
- The seller must still be live on the marketplace
- Your account must not be on hold with this seller
- Cannabis orders must be within the same state (state restriction check)
- All items must have available inventory
- Order minimums must be met
- On-deck inventory rules must be satisfied (see Browse Marketplace and Add Items)

**Optional fields** (applied to all orders created from this cart):
- `buyer_note`: note attached to the order
- `shipping_method`: shipping method for the order
- `ship_name`, `ship_line_one`, `ship_line_two`, `ship_city`, `ship_state`, `ship_zip`, `ship_country`: shipping address override. If omitted, defaults from your company are used.

On success, the cart is deleted and inventory is deducted from batches.

Requires marketplace API access to be enabled for your company. This is not enabled by
default — contact support to enable marketplace ordering.

get.description:
**Required ability:** `view:receiving-orders`

A receiving order is for the purchaser.

- `seller_company_id`: the company_id of the seller
- `buyer_id`: the seller's CRM relation of the buyer

**Order Item Information:**
- `order_quantity` paired with `order_unit_measurement` determines sales quantities. Eg 5 2gram packs, or 3 cases (units_per_case of 3).
- `inventory_quantity` paired with `unit_measurement` determines base units of measure.
- `unit_size_unit_measurement` is available on some categories for single unit sizes.

`updated_at_from` is a required filter.

**Required ability:** `view:shipping-orders`

A shipping order belongs to the seller on an order.

- `buyer_company_id`: the company_id of the purchaser
- `buyer_id`: the seller's CRM relation of the buyer
- `order_status_id`: the status of an order. Note that this status is dynamic. See the Deal Flow documentation.

**Order Item Information:**
- `order_quantity` paired with `order_unit_measurement` determines sales quantities.
- `inventory_quantity` paired with `unit_measurement` determines base units of measure.
- `unit_size_unit_measurement` is available on some categories for single unit sizes.
- `order_sales_unit_listing_price` gives you the original listing price of the batch.

`updated_at_from` is a required filter.

get.description:
**Required ability:** `view:shipping-orders`

Returns all carts belonging to the authenticated API token. Optionally filter by `buyer_id`
to find carts for a specific buyer.

NOTE: This is not making available carts that are shown in the storefront to buyers or sellers. Carts here are specifically API only carts.

- `buyer_id`: (optional) filter to only return carts for this buyer

**Required ability:** `view:shipping-orders`

Returns the cart with full pricing calculations, grouped by seller operation (each group
becomes a separate order on conversion). Includes per-item pricing, subtotals, and
availability status.

**On-deck warnings:** Items from on-deck batches (`hold = true`) are flagged with
`on_deck_warning: true` and an explanatory message in two situations:
- off-deck inventory for the same product still has unclaimed quantity, or
- a lower-`sort_order` on-deck batch for the same product still has unclaimed quantity.

Off-deck batches must be fully consumed (in the DB or in this cart) before any on-deck
batch is purchased, and on-deck batches must be consumed in ascending `sort_order`.

**Availability flags:** Items may include `unavailable` or `stockIssue` flags if batch
inventory has changed since the item was added. Review these before converting.

**Order minimums:** Sellers can configure minimum order values per operation, either as a
total dollar amount or per product category. If minimums are not met, the response includes
a `minimums` object keyed by operation ID, showing the minimum type, required amount, and
(for category minimums) which categories are short. The cart cannot be converted until
minimums are satisfied.

delete.description:
**Required ability:** `create:shipping-orders`

Permanently deletes the cart and all its items. This action cannot be undone.

post.description:
**Required ability:** `create:shipping-orders`

Adds one or more items to a cart for the given buyer. If no cart exists for this buyer
and API token, one is created automatically. Each API token can have one active cart per buyer.

Items can be specified by batch or by product. All items are validated and added atomically —
if any item fails validation, none are added.

**Choosing between batch-level and product-level allocation:**

- **Batch-level (`batch_id`)** gives the caller full control over which specific batches end
  up on the order. Use this when the buyer cares about per-batch attributes (COA, terpene
  profile, potency, harvest date, lot number, brand, operation/location) or when the price
  matters precisely — pricing is defined per batch, so the unit price for a given product
  can differ batch to batch. The caller is responsible for following the inventory rules
  below (off-deck before on-deck, then sort_order within each pool).
- **Product-level (`product_id`)** is the simpler path: the API allocates the requested
  quantity across the product's eligible batches automatically, draining off-deck batches
  in `sort_order` first and falling through to on-deck only if off-deck cannot fulfill the
  request. **Use with caution:** sellers may use non-standard batch conventions (e.g.
  different flavors per batch), so the allocated mix may not be what the buyer would have
  picked by hand. Pricing is defined per batch on all products, so when the allocation
  spans multiple batches the resulting cart lines can each have a different unit price
  even though the buyer asked for a single product at a single unit. The response returns
  the resulting cart with each allocated batch and its details; callers should inspect it
  before converting.

**Inventory rules (important):**

Sellers split inventory into two pools per product:
- **off-deck** batches (`hold = false`) are in stock and sell first
- **on-deck** batches (`hold = true`) are reserved and may only be sold once off-deck is exhausted

Within each pool, batches have a `sort_order` that defines the consumption sequence.
When building an order, you must:

1. Call **Available Inventory** with `include_batches=true` to see each batch's `hold` and
   `sort_order`.
2. Add all off-deck batches with available inventory before adding any on-deck batch.
3. Add on-deck batches in ascending `sort_order` — you may not skip ahead to a later on-deck
   batch while an earlier one still has unclaimed inventory.

The cart accepts on-deck items eagerly but flags `on_deck_warning: true` on any line that
violates these rules. The **Convert Cart to Orders** endpoint enforces the rules strictly
and returns `422` with a `violations` array if they are not satisfied.

**By `batch_id`:** Adds a specific batch to the cart. The batch must belong to the authenticated
company, not be archived or permanently held, be assigned to an operation, and have available
inventory (unless inventory tracking is disabled). The inventory check sums consumption across
all cart lines for the batch (each multiplied by its variant's `base_unit_multiple`) and
rejects the add if it would exceed the batch's stock.

**By `product_id`:** Automatically allocates the requested quantity across the product's eligible
batches, filling off-deck inventory before on-deck and following `sort_order` within each pool.
Creates one cart item per allocated batch. Fails if total available inventory is insufficient.

Each item requires either `batch_id` or `product_id` (not both).

- `buyer_id`: the buyer this cart is for. Must belong to the authenticated company and not be on hold or disabled.
- `items`: array of items to add
- `items.*.batch_id`: specific batch to add (use this or `product_id`). Follow the inventory rules above.
- `items.*.product_id`: product for auto-allocation across batches (use this or `batch_id`)
- `items.*.quantity`: amount to add. If the same (batch, sample, unit) combo already exists in the cart, the quantity is added to the existing item. Different units on the same batch produce separate cart lines, and the inventory check sums base-unit consumption across all of them.
- `items.*.order_unit_measurement_id`: the unit of measurement for ordering (e.g. Case, Unit, Gram). Must match a valid pricing variant for the batch/product. Available variants are returned by the Available Inventory endpoint when `include_batches` is `true`.
- `items.*.sample`: when `true`, the item is marked as a sample. Sample and non-sample items for the same batch produce separate cart lines. Samples consume from the batch's inventory only when the batch is configured with `track_sample_quantity = true`.

delete.description:
**Required ability:** `create:shipping-orders`

Removes one or more items from the cart by cart item ID. The entire item is removed
regardless of quantity — there is no partial quantity removal. Use Add Items to adjust
quantities by removing and re-adding.

Cart item IDs are returned on every line in the View Cart and Add Items responses
(`data.cart_items.*.id`). Use those values here. A single batch can produce multiple cart
lines — separate lines for sample vs. non-sample, and a separate line per unit of measure
on Pack To Order products — so identifying lines by `id` is the only way to remove one
line surgically without touching its siblings.

- `items`: array of items to remove
- `items.*.id`: the cart item id to remove

message.const: No matching items found in cart

post.description:
**Required ability:** `create:shipping-orders`

Converts the cart into one or more orders. Items are grouped by seller operation — each
group becomes a separate order. All orders are created atomically: if any order fails,
the entire conversion is rolled back.

**Pre-conversion validation:**
- The seller company must be approved, not on hold, not disabled, and have a seller subscription
- The buyer must not be on hold
- Cannabis orders must be within the same state (state restriction check)
- All items must have available inventory (no `unavailable` or `stockIssue` flags)
- Order minimums must be met
- **On-deck rules:** an on-deck batch (`hold = true`) may only be converted when (a) all off-deck
  inventory for the same product has been either depleted or fully claimed in this cart, and
  (b) every lower-`sort_order` on-deck batch for the same product has been either depleted or
  fully claimed in this cart. Use the **Available Inventory** endpoint with `include_batches=true`
  to plan the order, and the **View Cart** response's `on_deck_warning` flag to catch violations
  before converting. Violations are returned in `violations` with a `reason` field of
  `off_deck_remaining` or `on_deck_sort_order`.

**Optional fields** (applied to all orders created from this cart):
- `buyer_note`: note attached to the order
- `shipping_method`: shipping method for the order
- `ship_name`, `ship_line_one`, `ship_line_two`, `ship_city`, `ship_state`, `ship_zip`, `ship_country`: shipping address override. If omitted, defaults from the buyer are used.

On success, the cart is deleted and inventory is deducted from batches.

get.description:
**Required ability:** `view:products`

Product types cannot be created through the API due to manual association needed for marketplace grouping.
Please reach out to support if you need a type created. Product Types belong to a Product Category.

**Required ability:** `view:products`

The inventory system has a parent child relationship. There is a parent product with many child batches.
The batches are connected to the parent through a `product_id` on the batch. Any prices added at the
product level will be used as the default prices for batches.

- `product_category_id`: the main category for the product, determines what fields will be available
- `product_type_id`: the subtype. For instance, if the category is flower, the type might be A-Bud
- `units_per_case`: if filled in, the product is sold in cases
- `units_per_package`: number of units in a single sellable package. Eg, 3 pack of joints
- `for_distributors`, `for_retailers`, `for_wholesalers`: booleans that mark the type of buyers that can see these products

**Measurements vary by category:**
- `product_unit_measurement_id`: the fundamental measurement, required for all products. For "Edibles & Drink, Topicals & Wellness, Tincture, Cartridge, Live Plant, Prepack, Preroll, Merchandise, Extract" use "Unit". For other categories use the appropriate unit (e.g., Pound for flower).
- `unit_size`: for categories sold in units (Cartridge, Merchandise, Edibles & Drink, Tincture, Extract, Topicals & Wellness). E.g., the '2' in a 2 gram cartridge.
- `unit_size_unit_measurement_id`: linked to `unit_size`. E.g., 'gram' in 2 grams.
- `packagedUnitSize`: see the /package-sizes endpoint. Used for Prepack.

**Important:** Do not rely on the `with_batches` option for building an inventory sync. An update to a
batch does not update the `updated_at` field on a product. Call both /products and /batches endpoints
separately with `updated_at_from`.

`updated_at_from` is a required filter. The first time you call this endpoint you should call it from the
date the company first joined, but subsequent calls should be restricted to only search for records updated
since the last call if possible.
